name: Cable Triceps Pushdown (Rope)
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and grip an end in each hand with thumbs up.
Stand tall, brace your core, and pin your elbows snugly to your sides.
Keeping the upper arms fixed, extend the elbows to drive the rope down and slightly apart at the bottom.
Pause briefly with arms fully straight and the triceps fully contracted.
Control the rope back up until your forearms are just above parallel, then repeat.
formCues: Keep elbows tucked and stationary throughout.
Spread the rope ends apart at lockout for a full contraction.
Move only at the elbow, not the shoulder.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows or letting them drift forward.
Using body english or leaning to push the weight down.
Cutting the range short at the top or bottom.

name: Overhead Cable Rope Triceps Extension
instructions: Set the pulley to a low or mid position, attach a rope, then face away from the stack.
Grip the rope and raise your hands overhead with elbows bent and pointing forward.
Stagger your stance and keep a tall torso with a slight forward lean for stability.
Extend your elbows to press the rope forward and up until your arms are fully straight.
Pause at lockout, then lower under control to a deep stretch behind your head and repeat.
formCues: Keep the upper arms still and high; hinge only at the elbows.
Feel a deep stretch in the long head at the bottom.
Keep your ribs down and core braced to protect the lower back.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide and drop on each rep.
Overarching the lower back to move heavier weight.
Shortening the range and skipping the stretch at the bottom.

name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher (Lying Triceps Extension)
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar over your chest with a shoulder-width grip.
Tilt your upper arms slightly back so the elbows point up and a touch behind you, not straight up.
Keeping the upper arms fixed, bend the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind your head.
Stop when you feel a strong triceps stretch, then extend the elbows to press the bar back up.
Lock out just short of full elbow extension to keep tension, then repeat.
formCues: Keep elbows pointing up and roughly shoulder-width.
Lower toward the top of the forehead or behind the head, not the face.
Control the eccentric; never let the bar drop.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows out, shifting load off the triceps.
Turning it into a pullover by moving the shoulders.
Using too much weight and losing the bar path near the face.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar slightly inside shoulder width, roughly 8 to 12 inches apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with wrists stacked over your elbows.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest while keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Lightly touch the chest, then press the bar back up by extending the elbows.
Lock out over the chest without flaring the elbows, then repeat.
formCues: Keep elbows tucked at roughly 30 to 45 degrees, not flared.
Grip just inside shoulder width; avoid a painfully narrow grip.
Drive through the bar to extend the elbows powerfully.
commonMistakes: Gripping too narrow, straining the wrists.
Flaring the elbows and turning it into a chest press.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.

name: Parallel Bar Triceps Dips
instructions: Grip parallel bars and press up to support yourself with arms straight and shoulders down.
Keep your torso as upright as possible to bias the triceps over the chest.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until your upper arms reach about parallel to the floor.
Keep your elbows tracking back and close, not flaring wide.
Press through your palms to extend the elbows and return to the locked-out start.
formCues: Stay upright with elbows tucked to emphasize the triceps.
Lower only to a comfortable shoulder depth (about parallel).
Keep your shoulders pulled down and back, away from your ears.
commonMistakes: Descending too deep and stressing the shoulders.
Flaring the elbows wide, shifting load and irritating the joints.
Shrugging the shoulders up at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
Brace your free hand on a bench and keep a flat, neutral back.
Raise your upper arm so the elbow is pinned alongside your torso, with the forearm hanging down.
Extend the elbow to straighten your arm fully, squeezing the triceps at the top.
Pause at lockout, then lower the forearm under control and repeat before switching sides.
formCues: Keep the upper arm fixed and parallel to the floor.
Fully straighten the arm and squeeze at the top.
Use light to moderate weight and control the lowering phase.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum.
Dropping the elbow so only the shoulder moves.
Rounding the back during the hinge.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Set up in a high plank and place your hands close together under your chest so thumbs and index fingers form a diamond.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward your hands, keeping the elbows tracking back close to your sides.
Stop just before your chest touches your hands, then press back up by extending the elbows.
Lock out at the top without letting your hips sag or pike, then repeat.
formCues: Keep elbows tucked toward your ribs, not flared out wide.
Maintain a rigid plank; do not let the hips drop or rise.
Drop to your knees to scale the movement if needed.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows out, shifting load to the shoulders.
Letting the hips sag and overarching the lower back.
Cutting the depth short and skipping the stretch.
